templates.name: Addition/similarity: a further item of the same kind
Contrast: established view or appearance, then a finding that breaks it
Contrast: positive claim, then a limiting fact about the same subject
Cause/effect: condition, principle or evidence, then its consequence
Cause/effect: need or judgment, then the action it motivates
Concession: grant, then the main claim resumes (but / Still)
Concession: supported claim, then a fact that qualifies it
Purpose and aptness: goal then deliberate act, or a fitting echo
Specification/restatement: exact content or plain rewording
Sequence/time: next step, earlier or later event, end of a long effort
Example: general claim, then one named instance

items.passage: Slack-key guitar is widely celebrated as one of the most distinctively Hawaiian musical traditions. ______ the guitar itself was an import, introduced by Mexican cowboys, or vaqueros, recruited in the 1830s to manage the islands’ expanding cattle herds. Still, slack key was a local innovation: Hawaiian players loosened, or “slacked,” the strings into open tunings of their own devising.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence calls slack-key guitar “one of the most distinctively Hawaiian musical traditions.” The blank sentence admits a fact that seems to cut against that claim: the guitar itself was “an import,” introduced by Mexican cowboys. The next sentence returns to the claim with “Still,” so “Of course” fits: it introduces a point the writer grants before turning back to the main claim.

A.why_wrong: The guitar’s arrival with Mexican cowboys is not an instance of slack key being distinctly Hawaiian; it is a point against that claim, which is why the next sentence has to answer it with “Still.”

B.why_wrong: The music’s reputation as Hawaiian does not lead to the fact that the guitar came from elsewhere; the two facts pull in opposite directions.

D.why_wrong: “In addition” would offer the guitar’s foreign origin as one more reason to call the music Hawaiian, but it is a reason to doubt that, as the turn with “Still” shows.

items.notes: Grant then turn, the turn opened by Still in the next sentence (3.19 shape), keyed Of course. K1 has no band-7 official items (spec/rw/band7/transitions.md section 5), so this is written as a strong band 6 and band_target is 6, not the 7 the plan asked for. Trap: For instance and In addition, for a reader who takes the blank sentence as support for the opening claim. No In fact, Indeed or Actually beside the concession key; no contrast decoy. Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Diamonds grown in laboratories have the same crystal structure and chemical makeup as diamonds mined from the earth, and even experienced jewelers cannot tell the two apart by eye. ______ gem-testing laboratories can usually identify a lab-grown stone, using instruments that detect growth patterns and traces of impurities that natural diamonds rarely share.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence stresses how alike lab-grown and mined diamonds are: “even experienced jewelers cannot tell the two apart by eye.” The blank sentence limits that point without overturning it: with the right instruments, gem-testing laboratories “can usually identify a lab-grown stone.” “Granted” introduces a fact that qualifies the claim just made.

B.why_wrong: “Moreover” would add a further point showing that the two kinds of diamond are alike, but the laboratories’ ability to identify lab-grown stones shows a difference between them.

C.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not spell out how the stones are alike; it names a way they can be told apart, an exception to the first sentence.

D.why_wrong: Laboratories that can tell the stones apart are not doing the same thing as jewelers who cannot; their success is the opposite of the jewelers’ failure.

items.notes: Supported claim, then a fact that limits it (3.8 shape), keyed Granted rather than That said (8 of 10 live K2 keys are That said). Band 6 by plan. No cause decoy, since a reader could take the instruments as the laboratories’ response to the stones looking alike; no In fact or Indeed (second-sense rule); no contrast decoy. Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Television footage typically depicts avalanches as immense walls of snow thundering down a mountainside unprompted, released by heavy snowfall or sudden warming. Investigators who reconstruct fatal avalanche accidents describe a less cinematic pattern; ______ the slide that buries a backcountry skier or snowmobiler is triggered not by the weather but by the victim or by another member of the victim’s party.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Television footage shows avalanches thundering down a mountainside “unprompted, released by heavy snowfall or sudden warming,” but investigators “describe a less cinematic pattern.” The clause after the blank gives that pattern: the slide that buries a skier or snowmobiler is triggered “by the victim or by another member of the victim’s party.” “More often” marks this as the usual case, compared with the natural releases the footage shows.

A.why_wrong: The investigators’ account does not make skiers trigger slides; the clause after the blank reports what the investigators find, not a result of their work.

C.why_wrong: The clause after the blank is not a second point added to the investigators’ pattern; it is the pattern itself, the less cinematic way most fatal slides begin.

D.why_wrong: A slide triggered by the victim does not qualify the “less cinematic pattern”; it is what makes the pattern less cinematic than the footage.

items.passage: Pacific salmon such as sockeye and chinook are semelparous: after migrating from the ocean upriver to spawn, they reproduce once and die. Steelhead, ______ are iteroparous; these sea-run rainbow trout undertake the same migration, but some survive spawning, return to the ocean, and reproduce again in subsequent years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says Pacific salmon such as sockeye and chinook are semelparous: they “reproduce once and die.” The blank sentence describes a second kind of fish, steelhead, that are iteroparous: some “reproduce again in subsequent years.” “In contrast” marks steelhead as the second subject, with the opposite trait.

A.why_wrong: Steelhead are not an instance of fish that spawn once and die; they are offered as fish that do the opposite.

B.why_wrong: Salmon dying after spawning is not a reason steelhead survive and spawn again; the two facts describe different fish.

C.why_wrong: Steelhead “undertake the same migration,” but what the sentence says about them, that some survive to spawn again, is the opposite of what the first sentence says about salmon.

items.passage: Mexican composer Carlos Chávez built his Sinfonía india (1936), a compact single-movement symphony, around melodies of Indigenous peoples of northern and western Mexico, among them Yaqui and Huichol songs. ______ in orchestrating the work, Chávez drew on the same traditions, calling for several Indigenous percussion instruments to be played alongside the orchestra’s own percussion section.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says Chávez built the Sinfonía india “around melodies of Indigenous peoples.” The blank sentence turns back to the same work and the same sources but adds a separate feature: “in orchestrating the work,” Chávez called for “several Indigenous percussion instruments.” “What’s more” introduces this second, additional way the symphony draws on Indigenous music.

A.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not give the exact content of the melodies the first sentence mentions; it turns from the melodies to the orchestration and names a different element of the work, the percussion instruments.

B.why_wrong: The instruments do not qualify or cut against the use of Indigenous melodies; they point the same way.

D.why_wrong: Although the blank sentence says Chávez “drew on the same traditions,” it does not reword the claim about the melodies; it adds new information about how he orchestrated the work.

items.passage: Chinese painters working in the gongbi style construct each image from fine, meticulously controlled outlines, which they fill with translucent layers of color, sometimes over several months. Practitioners of the xieyi style, ______ work rapidly with loose, expressive brushstrokes, seeking to capture the spirit of a subject rather than its precise appearance.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence describes gongbi painters, who work slowly from “fine, meticulously controlled outlines.” The blank sentence describes a second group, xieyi painters, who “work rapidly with loose, expressive brushstrokes.” “By contrast” signals that the second style is the opposite of the first.

B.why_wrong: The sentence about xieyi painters does not reword the description of gongbi; it describes a different style.

C.why_wrong: The slow, careful method of gongbi painters is not what makes xieyi painters work quickly; the two groups simply work in opposite ways.

D.why_wrong: Xieyi is not one more example of the careful method just described; it departs from that method.

items.notes: Two subjects, opposite values, blank as an interrupter after the second subject (2.6 position, 2.4 parallel build). Decoys from three other families, none a parallel word. items.passage: The spotted lanternfly, an invasive planthopper, was first detected in Pennsylvania in 2014. It debilitates grapevines and numerous other plants by extracting their sap. ______ the insects excrete a sugary residue called honeydew, which promotes the growth of a black, sooty mold that coats foliage and interferes with photosynthesis.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence names one way the spotted lanternfly harms plants: by “extracting their sap.” The blank sentence names a second harm: the honeydew the insects excrete promotes a mold that “coats foliage and interferes with photosynthesis.” “Moreover” adds this further point to the first.

A.why_wrong: The honeydew and mold are not a particular case of extracting sap; they are a separate kind of damage.

B.why_wrong: The insects do not excrete honeydew in place of extracting sap; they do both, and both harm the plants.

C.why_wrong: “Regardless” would treat the sap feeding as beside the point, but the blank sentence adds to it rather than setting it aside.

items.notes: Two harms of one pest, independent and pointing the same way (2.10 shape: two harms of wishcycling). No cause decoy, since honeydew is itself a by-product of sap feeding and Thus could be argued; no Meanwhile, which could read as at the same time. items.passage: The hornet moth, widespread throughout Europe, cannot sting. Its transparent wings and yellow-and-black striped abdomen, however, make it resemble a hornet so convincingly that birds generally avoid it. ______ the wasp beetle, a stingless longhorn beetle common in European gardens, deters predators with conspicuous black and yellow bands and rapid, jerky movements.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence describes the hornet moth, a harmless insect that resembles a hornet “so convincingly that birds generally avoid it.” The blank sentence describes a second harmless insect, the wasp beetle, that also wards off predators by resembling a wasp. “Likewise” signals that the wasp beetle does the same thing as the hornet moth.

A.why_wrong: Nothing in the blank sentence is conceded against the point about the hornet moth; the wasp beetle supports the same pattern.

C.why_wrong: The wasp beetle is not an instance of the hornet moth; it is a different insect doing the same thing, a parallel case rather than an example.

D.why_wrong: The hornet moth’s disguise does not cause the wasp beetle’s; the two insects protect themselves the same way independently.

items.explanation: The second sentence makes a general claim: the entrances reflect “a fascination with organic, botanical forms.” The blank sentence spells out exactly what those forms are: railings that “rise like the stalks of plants” and lamps that “resemble drooping flower buds.” “Specifically” introduces these precise details.

B.why_wrong: The details in the blank sentence agree with the sentence before it; nothing in them contrasts with forms taken from nature.

B.why_wrong: The dating results are not an example of the old assumption; they are evidence against it.

C.why_wrong: The belief that Iron Age people made the horse did not lead the dating to show that it is older; the finding contradicts the assumption.
